MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  January 26, 2021
Due to COVID-19 and the “Stay at Home” Order for the State of California and the Social
Distance Guidelines issued by Federal, State, and Local Authorities this Council Meeting was
conducted via Video Teleconferencing for all Council and Staff with the exception of the City
Attorney and City Clerk who were present in the Council Chamber. All public comments that
were emailed to the City Clerk were read during the meeting.

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library
Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Kelley at
5:01 p.m., on January 26, 2021, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by
5:00 p.m. on January 21, 2021, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted
at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Teleconferenced:  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Raths
  Council Member Sachs
  Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum
  Mayor Kelley

Absent:  None

Staff  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
Teleconferenced:  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services

Staff Present:  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk
  Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel - Anticipated Litigation: Initiation of Litigation
  Pursuant to Paragraph (4) of Subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9 (2 cases)

City Council Minutes  1  January 26, 2021
 RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:02 p.m., Mayor Kelley recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:09 p.m. with five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that there was one Closed Session with two elements. The
City Council was given an update and he received some direction. No reportable action was
taken.

INVOCATION: Mayor Kelley

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Raths

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Featured Business of the Month – Menchie’s Frozen Yogurt

  Mayor Kelley presented a proclamation to business owners Antonio and Isabel Torrez.

P2. Diversity and Inclusion Task Force Update

  Received update from Director of Recreation and Community Services Mark Nix and
  residents Brian Tademy and Grant Voss.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

George Upegui, M.V.: Raised concerns regarding the heavy increase in Amazon fleet traffic on
Los Alisos and Peter Harman Way. Asked that the City consider conducting a traffic study.

Casey Ackerman, M.V.: Expressed concerns with the political campaign sales booths within the
City.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  City Council Minutes

City Council Minutes  2  January 26, 2021
   Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of January 12, 2021, as
  presented.

2.  Check Register Dated December 25, 2020 in the Amount of $1,399,427.90

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  Check Register Dated January 8, 2021 in the Amount of $2,622,073.87

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Quarterly Financial Report for the City of Mission Viejo - First Quarter 2020/21

  Received and filed.

5.  Contract for replacement of exterior doors and installation of new sliding interior door
  at the Oso Creek Golf Course Clubhouse.

  Approved contract for the replacement of exterior doors and installation of new sliding interior
  door at the Oso Creek Golf Course Clubhouse to SAS Construction (A21-02) for the period
  of February 1, 2021 through June 30, 2021, in an amount not to exceed $85,065.57.

6.  First Amendment to Affordable Housing and CDBG Loan Agreement between the
  Mission Viejo Housing Authority and Families Forward

  Approved First Amendment to Affordable Housing and CDBG Loan Agreement between
  the Mission Viejo Housing Authority and Families Forward.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

7.  Transportation Corridor Agency (TCA) Report

  Received report from Mayor Kelley.

8.  Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) Report

  Received report from Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum.

9.  Orange County Local Agency Formation Commission (LAFCO) Report

  Council Member Bucknum announced that there was nothing to report.

10. Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA) Report

City Council Minutes  3  January 26, 2021
   Received report from Council Member Goodell.

CITY MANAGER REPORT

City Manager Dennis Wilberg thanked Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum for all her hard work on the
Regional Housing Needs Assessment (RHNA) Appeals Board. Announced that the Regional
Council will be voting to take on the State thanks to the letter writing campaign that Council
Member Goodell and Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum started. He stated that the City is working with
the County to set up vaccination sights within the City at Saddleback College and possibly the
Norman P. Community Center. The County right now is focused on the super sights and Soka
University opened last Saturday with several employees having volunteered.

CITY ATTORNEY REPORT

City Attorney Bill Curley assured the public that the Council and Staff is not supportive or pleased
with the sidewalk vendors. He stated that the State Legislature through SB946 which essentially
stripped all cities in the State with the ability to regulate licenses or permits to street side vendors.
He mentioned that the City has started enforcement by using an extension of blinder-rack
regulations to obscure portions of harmful materials particularly from a child’s standpoint. The
vendors have upped their game on their booths with signage that takes them out of their sidewalk
vendor world and takes them into a different form or construct of what they are doing. We can’t
regulate what they say but can regulate secondary aspects of it, which may be affective in addressing
the concerns. Lastly, he stated that the City is not condoning any of this and is working to respect
the First Amendment Law with what Sacramento did to us with the passage of SB946, and despite
our hands being tied we are still working to get to a good point for the community.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

11. Investment Advisory Commission Appointment

  Council Member Goodell postponed his appointment to the next City Council Meeting.

12. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Goodell

13. The Death of Local Control: Join Us and Your Peers to Help us Prevent It

  Council Member Goodell gave his report.

  Motion made by Council Member Goodell, seconded by Mayor Kelley, to adopt Resolution
  21-02 Expressing Support for Actions to Further Strengthen Local Democracy, Authority,
  and Control as Related to Local Zoning and Housing Issues.

City Council Minutes  4  January 26, 2021
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths announced that he attended the Chamber of Commerce Day Breaker
breakfast this morning via Zoom. He indicated that the Chamber is very appreciative to the City
for the small business grants. Voiced concern of businesses closing in the City due to the closures.
He stated that we will get through this together and the City will continue to work with our
businesses to get through this epidemic.

Council Member Sachs

14. Consideration of a Promotional Effort Whereby Each Mission Viejo Household Would
  be Given up to $50 in Return for their Support of Mission Viejo Restaurants and Retail
  Establishments, Especially Mom and Pop Businesses, as they Struggle Through the
  COVID Crisis

  Council Member Sachs gave his report.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, to authorize
  the City to send a letter and $50 coupon to every household in the City to be redeemed at local
  businesses. At the end of 30 days the businesses will turn the coupons into the City for
  reimbursement and then another 15 days will be provided for any latecomers for a total of 45
  days. The final product of this program will come back at the next City Council Meeting.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

Council Member Sachs announced he got his COVID vaccination. Indicated that he was at an
elderly care facility and was very touched by the love that the care staff had for the residents
while they were waiting for their vaccines. He said it was very moving.

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum thanked Council Member Sachs for bringing the promotional efforts to
help Mission Viejo Businesses. She addressed that the street vendors are as a result of the State law
and she pointed out that the city does not issue business licenses. Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum gave
a big thank you to Karen Hamman for all the work she has done for the City. She has been a steady
force for the City, Council Members and Commissioners. Karen is the tapestry that pulls all the
threads together and has done a beautiful service to our residents with timely information on the
City Council Minutes  5  January 26, 2021
 city’s website and social media. Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum stated that she is a better Council
Member because of Karen and she wishes her the best in her retirement. Lastly, she asked staff
when outdoor dining will reopen at the Oso Creek Golf Club. Director of Public Services Keith
Rattay announced that outdoor dining at the golf course will open back up next Monday.

Mayor Kelley

Mayor Kelley announced that there will be a formal presentation to Karen Hamman at the February
9 City Council Meeting. She reminded residents to go online to othena.com to register to received
the COVID vaccination. Mayor Kelley stated that the problem with opening up more vaccination
locations, is not the availability of the locations but the insufficient supply of vaccinations. As more
vaccinations become available we hope to be able to serve more people. She announced that the
City did sponsor an additional blood Drive on January 19 because of the need for blood. It was
well attended with 50 pints of blood collected, and stated that each pint of blood can save up to
three lives. Mayor Kelley said that there will be another blood drive at the City in March, but that
the Elks Club will be hosting one February 4 and the Islamic Foundation will also be hosting one
on February 7. She shared that she received a note from Orange County Red Cross Vice President
David Engwall stating “2020 was a year unlike any other. During an unprecedented pandemic and
in the face of back to back disasters both locally and nationally, our team did what they always do,
they turned challenges into opportunities.” She stated that these times give us opportunities as well.
Mayor Kelley reminded residents to support Mission Viejo businesses. Mayor Goodell asked if he
could make an announcement that the City is sponsoring a virtual Fair Housing Workshop next
Tuesday, February 2 from 1:30 to 3:00 p.m. for anyone interested. Interested residents can go to the
City’s website to sign up.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:06 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Kelley adjourned the meeting in memory of long-time Mission Viejo resident John Alesi,
to Tuesday, February 9, 2021, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________
Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of February 9, 2021

City Council Minutes  6  January 26, 2021
